results.title: US, Ukraine say Europe to join peace talks as Putin sticks to hardline stance
results.content: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday, November 12, Europe would join the next round of talks with Russia, as Vladimir Putin indicated Moscow will not compromise on its hardline demands to end almost five years of war. In a packed day of shuttle diplomacy following negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Zelensky in Dublin.

results.title: Fallout from Nvidia scandal spreads as Huang resigns
results.content: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. The news wiped 4.3% of Nvidia’s share price by closing bell Thursday, while the scandal has also raised concerns over security in the United States, with the spotlight falling on US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

results.title: Peruvians flock to see Pope Leo XIV in city he served as bishop
results.content: Crowds in Peru's northern city of Chiclayo gathered early on Friday, November 13, ​ahead of ‌Pope Leo's arrival for the centerpiece event of his 12-day South America tour, an outdoor ⁠Mass with the people who called him their bishop for eight years. He declared on November 11 that the country where he served as a missionary for about 20 years was his homeland.

results.title: Microsoft faces a major Outlook outage: ‘no signs of a cyberattack’
results.content: Microsoft said "malicious" activity was not to blame for an Outlook outage that left users around the world without its crucial services on Friday, November 13, but reported making headway in fixing the massive disruption. Businesses, governments and likely millions of individuals have been without services like Outlook email for over half a day, triggering wide-ranging consequences.

results.title: France remembers victims of 2015 Paris terror attacks
results.content: France on Friday marks 11 years since the 2015 Paris terror attacks, in which more than 130 were killed as gunmen and suicide bombers attacked the Bataclan concert hall, a major stadium, restaurants and bars. France 24’s James André reports from outside the Bataclan where a tribute to the victims is being held.

results.title: Guinea opens illegal gold mining trial, 1,200 people arrested
results.content: Guinea opened a trial over illegal gold mining on Thursday, November 12, after a crackdown on mineral extraction in the district of Siguiri. There was a ban on "unregulated and illegal" gold mining in the area where the military was subsequently deployed. Security forces have expelled tens of thousands of foreign nationals who had come to work in the region's mines.

results.title: 'No war, no peace' situation between US and Iran 'cannot continue', Iraqi FM says
results.content: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said the "no war and no peace" situation in the region "cannot continue". He also said that closing all but two border crossings with Iran, as Washington demands, was "not possible". Finally, he confirmed that Iraqi oil now is now flowing through the Strait of Hormuz under US protection.

results.title: Toera's homecoming: Madagascar's slain king joins his ancestors after 129 years
results.content: In 1897, French colonial troops killed King Toera, ruler of Madagascar's powerful Sakalava kingdom of Menabe, and took his skull to Paris, where it remained hidden in a museum for more than a century. France returned the remains last year, and for the first time since his death, King Toera took his place among his ancestors during the Sakalava people's most sacred ritual.

results.title: Amnesty criticises South Sudan, UN over failure to heed massacre warnings
results.content: Amnesty International said Thursday, November 12, that South Sudan and UN peacekeepers failed to act on warnings of a massacre that ended with more than 200 dead in March. The world's youngest country has been plagued by civil war, poverty, corruption and intercommunal violence since it was formed in 2011. FRANCE 24 spoke to Donatella Rovera, Senior crisis response adviser at Amnesty International.

results.title: 'Big development' in peace talks as Ukraine says Europe to join Russia negotiations
results.content: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday Europe would join the next round of talks with Russia, as Vladimir Putin indicated Moscow will not compromise on its hardline demands to end almost five years of war. Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Zelensky in Dublin. France 24's Andrew Hilliar has the details.

results.title: As world gripped by climate emergency, COP31’s empty chairs signal low ambitions
results.content: It is the recurring theme of every speech at the COP summits: the urgent need to act in the face of increasingly frequent climate disasters. Yet this year’s conference in Turkey seems to have little ambition, as reflected in the low turnout and the host country’s own contradictions. Morgan Ayre has the story.

results.title: Potential 'national security crisis' as Nvidia ex-CEO summoned by US Congress
results.content: What began as an investigation into the now former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is turning into what could be shaping up to be a "national security crisis", says France 24's correspondent in Los Angeles Wassim Cornet, after US lawmakers called on Huang to face their questions in December. Huang resigned as head of the chip giant over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia's market valuation.

results.title: 'One of the biggest outages ever': Disruption to Microsoft services enters second day
results.content: An outage of Microsoft services such as Outlook, Teams and Copilot that began on Thursday continued to cause disruption to users around the world on Friday as the tech giant struggled to fix server problems it blamed for the problems. France 24’s tech correspondent Peter O’Brien takes a look at what we know about the outage which, given its scale and duration, makes it one of the “biggest ever”, he says.

results.title: Winter is coming: Putin seeks to 'hammer Ukrainians, their power grid, their water supplies'
results.content: As renewed diplomatic efforts seek to bring an end to Russia's war on Ukraine, the prospect of a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Russia's irreconcilable territorial demands, competing visions of European security and an increasingly unpredictable and pro-Moscow US. For Mark Galeotti, Executive Director of Mayak Intelligence and Honorary Professor at University College London's School of Slavonic and East European Studies, Moscow's maximalist vision conceals a more complex negotiating strategy. And the territorial dispute over Donbas presents a particularly formidable obstacle. Putin's determination to claim control over the entirety of the region confronts Ukraine's refusal to surrender territory it continues to hold.

results.title: 🔴 Live: Microsoft 'not aware of any malicious activity' behind global Outlook outage
Who will inherit 007's licence to thrill? 'The world is not enough' in the hunt for James Bond
results.content: More than six decades after James Bond first appeared on the big screen, the search for Daniel Craig's successor has become a revealing debate about the future of one of cinema's most enduring, and endearing, franchises. "From the cold-blooded sexual magnetism of Sean Connery to the more tongue-in-cheek take of Roger Moore, to Daniel Craig's gritty realism, there's really a James Bond for everyone." But who will inherit the licence to thrill? FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell takes us on this exciting edge-of-your-seat adventure with a "view to a kill". Should Bond remain faithful to his traditional identity, or reinvent himself to reflect changing attitudes towards gender, diversity and contemporary heroism?

results.title: AFCON 2027 qualifiers: Top guns Senegal, Cameroon, Ivory Coast deliver
results.content: Africa's heavyweights are delivering in the 2027 AFCON qualifiers. Senegal marked Patrick Vieira's first home game with an emphatic win over Sudan, while Cameroon and Ivory Coast took further steps towards qualification.

results.title: Live: Local services, schools hit by global Microsoft outage as disruption continues
results.content: Microsoft's Outlook email service has been disrupted since late Thursday as the tech giant struggles to fix issues with its servers, hitting businesses and government agencies that use the popular work platforms in 74 countries and territories. The company said Friday it had not found any malicious activity causing the outage and blamed elevated infrastructure loads. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

results.title: Pope Leo XIV meets abuse victims in Peru, says Church must make 'amends'
results.content: Pope Leo XIV met six victims of clerical abuse in Peru on Thursday, including people linked to disbanded group Sodalitium Christianae Vitae. The US-born pontiff also urged the Catholic Church to make amends to survivors and strengthen protections against abuse as he returned to the country where he served as a missionary and bishop for nearly two decades.

results.title: Haitian police retake national stadium after two years of gang control
results.content: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main football stadium Thursday after two years under gang control, with Salvadoran troops taking over security at the venue. El Salvador deployed 2,000 soldiers to Haiti following an ambush that left four of its troops missing.

results.title: Ukraine live: EU top diplomat Kallas warns Europe not to fall into Russia's 'traps'
results.content: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Friday that Europe must not walk into Russian "traps" as it takes a seat at the table in talks to end the war in Ukraine, adding that a ceasefire is still the top priority. European representatives will be included in the next round of talks between Russia and Ukraine after being left out of Abu Dhabi negotiations earlier this week. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

results.title: ‘Peruvian pope’ Leo XIV comes home to a country that shaped his life and faith through 'hardship'
results.content: François Picard is pleased to welcome Victor Casallo, Director of the Department of Philosophical and Theological Studies at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University. Can a Pope shaped by Peru's history of political violence, social inequality and religious activism help a deeply polarized nation heal and rediscover the possibility of dialogue? "We tend to see the other person not as someone who holds a different opinion, but as an enemy." Casallo argues that Pope Leo, the first American-born pontiff's identity cannot be understood through his Chicago origins alone.

results.title: ‘Peruvian pope’ Leo XIV comes home to a country that shaped his life and faith through 'hardship'
results.content: François Picard is pleased to welcome Victor Casallo, Director of the Department of Philosophical and Theological Studies at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University. Can a Pope shaped by Peru's history of political violence, social inequality and religious activism help a deeply polarized nation heal and rediscover the possibility of dialogue? "We tend to see the other person not as someone who holds a different opinion, but as an enemy." Casallo argues that Pope Leo, the first American-born pontiff's identity cannot be understood through his Chicago origins alone. His decades of pastoral experience in Peru, amid political instability, terrorism, state violence and profound social inequalities, have shaped a religious outlook rooted in cultural openness, solidarity with the marginalized and an intimate understanding of human suffering.

results.title: New York building collapse kills eight, including two children
results.content: Eight people, including two children, were killed when a residential building collapsed into an adjacent construction site in Brooklyn on Wednesday. Firefighters spent hours searching the rubble overnight before declaring the operation over on Thursday as authorities launched an investigation into the disaster.
